data.why: The app ships a built-in synthetic sample it loads with no upload, plus a real raw GBIF tab-separated export (gbif_test.csv.txt) to exercise the Darwin Core harmonization path; qc_test_survey.csv is a hand-written standard-schema CSV with a missing coordinate, a missing species name, zero coordinates, out-of-range latitude/longitude, a non-numeric abundance value, and an extreme abundance outlier, to exercise the quality-control quarantine logic on the plain-CSV path (which the GBIF file alone does not cover).

goals: Load my own field survey CSV (or the built-in demo) and see it harmonized to Darwin Core fields automatically
Find out which records were flagged or quarantined by the QC audit (missing coordinates, invalid lat/lon, zero coordinates, missing taxon) and what my overall data usability score is
Compute Shannon-Wiener, Simpson, Pielou evenness and Margalef diversity indices per site and at the landscape level
Explore sampling sites on an interactive map, colored by diversity status, to spot which sites look species-poor
Set my own Shannon-Wiener and richness screening thresholds and see which sites get flagged for follow-up review
Generate and download a text screening report summarizing the data, methods, and flagged sites

review.summary: The tree follows the app's real path from loading data through QC counts, diversity indices, map, thresholds and report, and every screen I opened matches its node; it also honestly records that the app never lists individual flagged records. A few small fixes are needed before filing: correct the per-site Margalef claim, fix t3's branch type, fold the generic table-toolbar task into t6, and add the missing diversity-index feature.
